newsitem.title: FRANCE: French say justice is under government thumb - poll.
newsitem.headline: French say justice is under government thumb - poll.

text.p: French voters are strongly critical of their justice system, with an overwhelming 82 percent convinced it is under the government's thumb, according to an opinion poll published by the Le Monde newspaper on Thursday.

The SOFRES poll for the daily and for RTL radio, was taken after a wave of political corruption scandals and showed 73 percent of those asked believed judges were more lenient towards politicians than to ordinary citizens.
Only 14 percent believed repeated assurances by justice ministers that political authorities did not lean on public prosecutors or seek to influence probes.
Sixty-nine percent believed senior civil servants also benefited from special treatment, with business leaders, doctors, police officers and journalists very far behind.

"This feeling of inequality in the face of the law is no doubt linked to the emergence of "scandals' which have brutally highlighted the political authorities' strong pressures on magistrates," Le Monde wrote.
"It is also no doubt based on the amnesties of 1988 and 1990, which exonerated actions linked to the funding of political parties," the newspaper said.

The survey was carried out on January 24-25, a few weeks after President Jacques Chirac called for greater independence for the judiciary, better protection of the presumption of innocence and simpler legal procedures.
Seventy-six percent of those polled said priority must be given to speeding up the legal process.

Safeguarding presumption of innocence was not a priority. For more than half those questioned, imposing total secrecy on investigations would be first and foremost "a way of preventing the media from reporting probes".

Socialist Michel Sapin, a former junior justice minister, has said that Chirac's sudden interest in justice reform was suspicious at a time when magistrates were investigating alleged kickbacks to his Gaullist RPR party while he was mayor of Paris in 1977-95.
